text:
Among the four customers represented in this log, **50% reported an export problem: 2 of 4 customers (A and B)**. This is a customer share of this log only, not a rate among all customers of the service.

Separately, export reports account for **3 of 6 ticket entries (50%)**: E1, E2 and E3. E1 and E2 concern the same event X, so they are two occurrences but only one distinct instance. The two percentages happen to match; their counting units differ.

| Wording group | Supporting entries | Occurrences | Distinct instances | Finding |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Export failed | E1, E2, E3 | 3 | 2: X and Y | Repeated reported problem; shared cause unknown |
| Login failed | E4 | 1 | 1: Z | Isolated signal |
| Display failed | E5, E6 | 2 | 1: Q | Isolated signal with a repeat report |

Confidence is high in these descriptive counts because the complete one-week log specifies customer and event identities. Confidence in any shared-cause finding is low: none of the six entries has a diagnosed cause or supporting diagnostic evidence. The shared word “failed” does not establish a common driver across export, login and display problems, nor does matching export wording establish the same cause for X and Y.

Cause-based grouping therefore remains unresolved. Diagnosis is needed before deciding whether a recurring driver warrants a fix. A person should check those diagnoses, assess significance and approve any resulting change.
